title: Understanding the Role of the Drain Trap
description: Every plumbing fixture connected to a drainage system requires a properly installed drain trap. The primary purpose of a trap is to hold a standing column of water, known as the water seal, which acts as a physical barrier preventing sewer gases, foul odors, and harmful bacteria from entering living spaces. Maintaining this seal depends on proper venting and trap design; if a trap loses its water due to evaporation, siphonage, or back-pressure, dangerous gases can escape indoors. Professional technicians always inspect traps and cleanout plugs during routine maintenance to ensure the integrity of the trap seal remains intact.
